'''Human replica droids''', or '''HRDs''' (sometimes referred to as "'''meatdroids'''" or "'''droid clones'''" or "'''Bobbie-Bots"'''), were sophisticated [[Droid/Legends|droids]] designed to be nearly indistinguishable from [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. 

Throughout galactic history, only a handful of such droids were known to have operated.<ref>''[[Shadows of the Empire: Evolution 1|''Shadows of the Empire: Evolution'' 1]]''</ref>
==Anatomy and technology==
[[File:GuriCreation-SotEE1.png|thumb|left|Guri, during her creation]]
Their design was similar to Human anatomy, with elaborate effort to fool most kinds of [[Medical scanner/Legends|medical scanners]]; their mechanical parts were carefully shielded.<ref name="sb" />

Strong alloys covered by [[Polymer/Legends|polymers]] served as [[Bone/Legends|bones]], with joints hiding thousands of concealed [[micro-gyro]]s; "organs" were made of [[biofiber]], including breathing [[lung/Legends|lungs]] and pumping [[heart/Legends|heart]]. The droid was covered with [[cloning/Legends|cloned]] vat-grown [[Synthskin/Legends|synthskin]].<ref name="sb">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

High-quality scanners (such as a [[Doppraymagno scanner]]) were able to discern some differences from the typical Human; although they wouldn't determine the droid as one, they could detect something vaguely odd. For example they would recognise the muscles as flesh not belonging to a known tissue.<ref name="sb" />

[[Guri]] had an [[AA-1 VerboBrain/Legends|AA-1 VerboBrain]], highly modified and expanded to include her programmed human behavior, and keeping track of Xizor's elaborate operations.<ref name="sb" />

Unlike true [[Cloning/Legends|clones]], a droid clone could be created in under three months. HRDs were programmed to think that they were real humans, even having fabricated childhood memories.

==History==
By [[19 BBY/Legends|18.8 BBY]], [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] of [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] had established a secret [[Abandoned droid factory|HRD laboratory]] in the abandoned [[Factory District]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Antipodes]] region. Xizor planned to subtly usurp control of Black Sun by replacing [[Underlord]] [[Dal Perhi]] with a [[Dal Perhi (droid)|HRD puppet]]. While Xizor considered the HRDs the first real advancement in droid manufacturing technology in a dozen centuries, his [[LeisureMech Enterprises/Legends|LeisureMech]]<ref name=":0">[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi (novel)'']]</ref> scientists were still many years away from perfecting it.<ref name=":1" /> The droid brain of his [[BB-3000]]<ref name=":0" /> HRD was somehow contaminated with the Perhi clone's genome. This resulted in the development of a strange hybrid virus that was partly RNA from the cloned tissue, and partly hardwired memetic algorithm from the substratum operating system. Xizor presented the HRD of Underlord Perhi to Black Sun operative [[Kaird]] to test if the HRD was convincing enough to fool someone familiar with the Underlord. During this meeting, the droid's hybrid virus caught it between two modalities of being, overloaded its sensorium circuitry, and caused its internal temperature to rapidly fluctuate until it melted. Once these issues were resolved, Xizor planned for his scientists to brainwash Kaird into launching a suicidal attack on Underlord Perhi. Xizor would then replace the dead Underlord with the HRD replacement. This plan could not be carried out as a pack of [[Feral droid|feral droids]] had torn Xizor's HRD laboratory apart and mutilated his scientists.<ref name=":1">[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight|''Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight'']]</ref>

LeisureMech eventually gave up on the genomic/algorithmic programming and cloned synthflesh organs of the BB-3000 series. They instead introduced the next generation of HRD: the [[BB-4000]]. They concentrated on neural net parallel processing, which greatly increased neural interaction and downgraded the development of killer memes. The downside was these new HRDs cost more and took longer to produce. LeisureMech risked everything on the success of their HRD series and went under when customers didn't take to them. The HRDs looked weird to customers because their skin was too uniform in shade. This caused customers to experience [[Eerie Coulee Disorder]], the pronounced sense of unease experienced by most humans and humanoids when they encountered a droid that appeared almost, but not quite, human. This ECD caused LeisureMech to go under, and forced them to sell off their remaining HRD stock.<ref name=":0" />            

Later HRD experiments included [[Project Decoy]], a plot by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] to create Rebel-controlled [[Human/Legends|Human]] replica droids used to replace [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]].<ref name="sb" /> Unfortunately for the Alliance, it lacked the necessary funding to continue the project. However, the Alliance did make at least one HRD, a [[Tardi (droid)|replica]] of [[Viscount (title)/Legends|Viscount]] [[Tardi]].
[[File:Human_replica_droid_TofG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A damaged HRD under fire.]]
The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]], managed to perfect HRD technology during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] when it hired designers [[Massad Thrumble]] and [[Simonelle]] the [[Ingoian]], who had stolen the technology from Confederate Holdouts and databases. They produced a Human replica droid named [[Guri]], later purchased as an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] by Prince Xizor of Black Sun for nine million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. Following this success, Simonelle relocated to the [[Minos Cluster/Legends|Minos Cluster]], establishing his own HRD [[Simonelle's workshop|workshop]], while Thrumble remained in Imperial service, [[Lexhannen Torlock (droid)|creating]] [[Frija Torlock (droid)|replicas]] of [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Lexhannen Torlock]] of [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]], and his daughter, [[Frija Torlock|Frija]]. These droids' self-awareness was so advanced that they ultimately rejected their programming as decoys, and fled to [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] to start a new life.

Simonelle attempted to create other droids like Guri, a possibily which Xizor considered undesireable. He sent Guri to the workshop to kill her own creator and ensure her uniqueness. Guri did not know that she actually killed [[Simonelle (droid)|a decoy]]; although Guri neglected destroying the workshop, along with the incomplete droids, Simonelle apparently chose to disappear, abandoning his project.<ref name="one">{{WEGCite|story=Only One of Her Kind|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref>

Following the [[Death/Legends|death]] of Xizor [[Battle over Coruscant|over]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Guri sought out her other creator, Thrumble, and asked for her memory to be purged of her assassination programming. The procedure, carried out on [[Hurd's Moon]], was a success, and Guri became a fully self-governing droid.<ref>''[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire: Evolution]]''</ref>

Approximately [[5 ABY/Legends|one year]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] completed Project Decoy, though its HRDs proved to be clumsy and inferior to Thrumble's designs. Project Decoy HRDs saw action in only a few missions, including one in which a [[Leia Organa II|duplicate]] of [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] helped kill the would-be [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Trioculus]].

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], [[Stanton Rendar|Dash Rendar]] set up an operation in the Minos Cluster to transfer the life-essence of paying customers into HRD bodies. He used the [[entechment]] technology pioneered by the [[Ssi-ruu|Ssi-Ruuk]], hoping that the procedure held the secret to eternal life.
